newsitem.title: SENEGAL: Workers disrupt international telecoms in Senegal.
newsitem.headline: Workers disrupt international telecoms in Senegal.

text.p: Workers at Senegal's telecommunications company SONATEL disrupted international telephone lines on Thursday to press demands linked to its privatisation, union leaders said.

The head of SONATEL union Ibrahima Konte told Reuters that staff being allocated a 10 percent stake in the capital of the company wanted to "benefit from 1996 dividents and also exoneration of tax on their stake".
Senegal sold one third of the state company on Monday to France Cables Radio, a subsidiary of France Telecom, for 650 million French francs ($107 miilion).

Many suscribers found international lines to Europe, particularly former colonial power France, blocked for voice, fax or data transmission on Thursday. "If a speedy solution is not found, the network will be further disrupted," Konte said.
The state will retain around a third of the capital, one third will go to Senegalese and foreign investors -- with 10 percent for staff and five percent to an African partner yet to be chosen.
